findings.name: Action Rehearsal Medal Tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold)
findings.detail: 5 Action Rehearsals exist (Swordfighter, Dashing Thief, Cowgirl, Kung Fu, Mighty), each a timed score-attack minigame unlocked after clearing that floor's boss. Each has Bronze/Silver/Gold score thresholds (e.g. Swordfighter/Kung Fu: Bronze 60+, Silver 100+, Gold 140+ points; Dashing Thief: Bronze 30+, Silver 70+, Gold 100+; Cowgirl/Mighty: lower thresholds, roughly Bronze 15-20+, Silver 30-40+, Gold 45-60+). Taking any damage ends the rehearsal. Gold rank on each rewards 60 coins plus an exclusive dress (e.g. Starry Dress, Checkered Dress, Heart Dress, Geometric Dress, Scaly Dress); Silver gives 30 coins; Bronze gives 10 coins.
findings.trackable: A 'Rehearsal High Score Leaderboard' is referenced by guides, implying the game stores and displays best score/rank per rehearsal, letting players see and replay to improve. Exact in-game screen name not independently confirmed beyond guide mentions.

findings.name: Sparkle Gems
findings.detail: 235 Sparkle Gems total: 220 from the 30 main story levels (10 gems in a level's first playthrough-equivalent slot structured as roughly 10 in the first play of an ensemble's level, 7 in the second, 5 in the third, totaling 22 per ensemble x 10 ensembles = 220), plus 15 more from post-game boss rematch challenges (5 bosses x 3 challenges each, 1 gem per challenge, first-time only).
findings.trackable: Collected count is tracked per level (visible when re-entering/selecting a level from the Theater Lobby, and shown at level-end results). Whether a single running game-wide total is displayed anywhere beyond per-level breakdown was not confirmed.

findings.name: Ribbons
findings.detail: 30 total Ribbons, one per main level (obtained by rescuing 'Ribboner' Theets, completing Action Rehearsals with Gold, or in some cases purchasable from the Floor 1 Shopkeep if missed during play). Each unlocks a costume/color for Stella or an outfit pattern.
findings.trackable: Ribbon collection status per level can be checked by re-entering the level from the Theater Lobby or via the pause menu inside a level.

findings.name: Outfits / Ensembles
findings.detail: 72 Peach and Stella outfit patterns/colors total (per Game8's 100% completion breakdown), purchasable with coins at the Lobby Shop once unlocked, or awarded from Gold rehearsal ranks and bosses.
findings.trackable: Viewable under 'Collection' from the Main Menu, which lists all transformation ensembles/outfits.

findings.name: Album Photos
findings.detail: 37 Album Photos total in the base completion list (30 base + 7 additional post-game photos including a final photo with Peach and Stella), earned by collecting all Sparkle Gems in a level and completing post-game boss challenges.

findings.name: Boss Rematches (Curtain Call structure)
findings.detail: After clearing the story (all 30 levels, 5 floor bosses + final boss Madame Grape), players return to Sparkle Theater where boss portraits appear on each floor allowing rematches. Each rematch offers 3 optional challenges (commonly 'take no damage' or 'don't hit X part' style), each rewarding 1 Sparkle Gem the first time completed (5 bosses x 3 = 15 gems). Madame Grape can be rebattled in the basement with her own 3 challenges.
findings.trackable: Challenge completion presumably tracked per boss encounter screen; not confirmed whether a global checklist exists.

findings.name: Hidden Theets (Hide-and-Seek / Ninja Sparkla students)
findings.detail: Post-game hide-and-seek content: reported as 70 hidden Theets across levels — described as 3 Theets hiding in each level on Floors 1-5 (30 levels) and 1 Theet in each Basement level. Framed as a Ninja Sparkla-themed challenge.
findings.trackable: Not confirmed whether the game shows a running count of Theets found per level or overall; guides imply per-level searches without a stated in-game counter.

findings.name: Sparkle Decorations
findings.detail: 15 Sparkle Decorations, purchasable post-game with Sparkle Gems from the Lobby Shop, used to decorate each of the 5 main floors of the Sparkle Theater (3 per floor; basement excluded).
findings.trackable: Presumably tracked via Lobby Shop purchase state.

findings.name: No selectable difficulty modes
findings.detail: The game has no difficulty mode selection. It is designed as a low-difficulty, story-focused experience. The one accessibility/assist element is the 'Heart Charm', an equippable item (obtainable by repeatedly talking to a Theet on Floor 1 who is struggling) that raises Peach's health from 5 hearts to 8 hearts, making the game easier. Ribbon/gem requirements are not affected by any difficulty toggle since none exists.

findings.name: No co-op or multiplayer mode
findings.detail: Princess Peach: Showtime! is a single-player only game. There is no local or online co-op/multiplayer mode. Some sources mention a 'shared Joy-Con' style assistance concept, but this is not a genuine second-player mode — it is unclear if this is even a real in-game feature versus a misremembered/conflated claim from a low-quality source.

findings.name: No known permanently missable content
findings.detail: All 30 main levels, and by extension their Sparkle Gems and Ribbons, remain freely replayable at any time via the Theater Lobby / floor select, both before and after story completion. Ribbons missed via the 'Ribboner' NPC can also be purchased later from the Floor 1 Shopkeep in some cases. No time-limited, demo-exclusive, or preorder-exclusive costume/content was found to be absent from or exclusive to the retail release; a free pre-launch demo existed but did not carry over exclusive unlockables into the full game as far as could be confirmed.
findings.trackable: Per-level completion (gems/ribbon obtained) can be checked by re-selecting the level from the lobby before entering.

findings.name: No significant RNG systems identified
findings.detail: No evidence found of randomized loot, enemy drops, shuffled puzzle solutions, or chance-based minigame outcomes. The game's levels, puzzles, and Action Rehearsal enemy patterns appear to be deterministic/fixed by design (side-scrolling stage-based platformer with authored puzzles).
sources: general search — no sources describing RNG mechanics found

findings.name: Single worldwide release, no major regional content differences found
findings.detail: Released simultaneously March 22, 2024 (some sources say March 15/21/22 depending on region) worldwide on Switch. No censorship or content-cut differences between Japanese and Western versions were found. Minor differences noted: box art facial expression changes between Japan and Western covers, and different fonts used for Korean/Chinese versions (cosmetic/localization only, not gameplay-affecting).

findings.name: No confirmed post-launch patches with content changes
findings.detail: Could not find any documented Switch patch notes beyond the Day One / base version (v1.0.0, March 2024 release). No evidence of a free content update adding new levels/costumes, nor of paid DLC ever being released for this game.

findings.name: Coins
findings.detail: A collective currency tally accumulated from level exploration, defeating enemies, popping balloons, etc. Used to purchase outfits/decorations and to skip levels or respawn at checkpoints. No fixed total count exists since coins are a spendable currency, not a finite collectible.
findings.trackable: Coin total is shown in the Lobby Shop / relevant purchase menus.

versionNotes.note: Single simultaneous worldwide Switch release (~March 2024); no confirmed platform-exclusive content since the game is Switch-exclusive with no other platform release.
No paid DLC exists for this game as of the last confirmed check.
No documented post-launch patch changed game content; could not rule out minor bugfix-only patches.
A free pre-launch demo existed (announced ~March 2024) but no evidence it left exclusive/missable content out of the full retail game.

gaps: Could not confirm whether the game displays a single aggregate 100% completion percentage anywhere (pause menu, main menu, or save select). Guides discuss '100% completion' as a community-defined checklist, not a stated in-game stat.
Could not verify the exact in-game name/location of the Action Rehearsal high-score/rank display screen (e.g. whether it's literally called a 'leaderboard' in-game or just a best-score readout).
Could not confirm whether Hidden Theets (post-game hide-and-seek, ~70 total) have any in-game counter, or whether this is purely a community-tracked collectible with no game-side confirmation UI.

Could not confirm exact per-rehearsal score thresholds for Cowgirl and Mighty rehearsals beyond an approximate range (45/60 for gold) — the source gave two numbers without clearly separating which rehearsal each applies to.

Could not confirm whether Ribbons obtained solely via Ribboner (not purchasable) are truly recoverable in 100% of cases, or whether a small subset are shop-exclusive/rehearsal-exclusive with no lobby purchase fallback.

Could not confirm the claimed 'shared Joy-Con' co-op-adjacent feature is a real mechanic in the shipped game rather than a conflated/incorrect claim from a low-quality source; treat as unconfirmed and likely non-existent.
Could not find dedicated patch notes source (e.g. Nintendo's own version history page) to confirm whether any bugfix-only updates were released post-launch.
Did not find any RNG system in the game; absence of evidence is not proof of absence, but no source described randomized mechanics of any kind.
